title: Who We Are
paragraphs: Axiorem is a software platform operated by Wellness Wizard Private Limited ("Axiorem", "we", "us", or "our").
Axiorem provides AI-native learning, training, document-processing, knowledge-management, assessment, workflow, and related services to individuals and Organizations.

For privacy purposes, the party responsible for processing personal data may depend on how the Service is used, the jurisdiction involved, and the relationship between Axiorem and the relevant Organization. This Privacy Policy explains Axiorem's own processing of personal data and the principal ways Axiorem processes information when providing the Service.

title: Scope of This Privacy Policy
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy applies to personal data processed through the Axiorem website, application, account systems, training platform, APIs, customer support channels, and related Service components that link to this Policy.

It applies to information you provide directly to Axiorem, information generated by use of the Service, and personal information that may be contained in Customer Content submitted by or on behalf of an Organization.

This Privacy Policy does not replace a separate enterprise Data Processing Addendum (DPA) where one is executed between Axiorem and a Customer. Where a DPA imposes specific obligations on Axiorem as a processor or service provider, the DPA controls to the extent of a conflict for the applicable processing.

Third-party websites, applications, LMS platforms, payment providers, identity providers, and other services may have their own privacy practices. Their policies apply to processing performed by those third parties.

title: Controller / Data Fiduciary and Processing Roles
paragraphs: Axiorem may act in different privacy roles depending on the processing activity.

For personal data relating to an individual's Axiorem Account, billing relationship, service usage, security, communications, and similar direct relationship, Axiorem may determine the purposes and means of processing and may therefore act as a controller, data fiduciary, or analogous role under applicable law.

Where an Organization uploads Customer Content containing personal data of employees, contractors, customers, learners, vendors, patients, or other individuals and instructs Axiorem to process that content to provide the Service, the Organization may remain the controller or data fiduciary and Axiorem may act as its processor, data processor, service provider, or analogous role, subject to applicable law and the relevant contractual arrangement.
The applicable allocation of roles should be documented in the Customer's DPA where required.

title: Information We Collect Directly From You
paragraphs: The exact information collected depends on how you use Axiorem.
Based on the current product design, Axiorem may directly receive and retain Account and identity information.
bullets: Google username or display name, where Google authentication is used.
Google OAuth or equivalent identity-provider identifier.
Profile picture or avatar, where supplied through the identity provider.
Organization, workspace, role, or subscription information where applicable.
Information you provide to customer support.
Information you voluntarily provide in forms, communications, or other interactions with the Service.

title: Customer Content and Information You Upload
paragraphs: Axiorem may process Customer Content that a User or Organization chooses to upload or otherwise provide through the Service.

Customer Content may include documents, PDFs, office files, policies, SOPs, manuals, handbooks, training material, technical documents, operational records, assessments, employee information, learner information, or other data that the Customer is authorized to process.

Because Customer Content is controlled by the Customer, Axiorem generally does not determine all of the personal-data categories contained within it. A document uploaded by an Organization could contain names, identifiers, employment information, contact information, training results, health and safety information, or other personal information depending on the Customer's own practices.
Customers should not upload information they are not legally or contractually permitted to provide to Axiorem.

title: Information We Collect Automatically
paragraphs: When you access or use the Service, Axiorem and its service providers may automatically collect certain technical and usage information necessary to operate, secure, troubleshoot, measure, and improve the Service.
Depending on the actual infrastructure, this may include:
bullets: Pages, screens, features, or endpoints accessed.
Cookie, local-storage, or similar technology identifiers.

title: Information We Receive From Third Parties
paragraphs: Axiorem may receive information from third parties when necessary to provide the Service.
Examples may include:
bullets: Identity providers such as Google when you authenticate through them.
Payment processors when you purchase a Subscription.
Cloud and security providers that transmit technical or security information to Axiorem.
LMS or integration partners when an Organization connects an external system.
Service providers that assist Axiorem with fraud prevention, abuse prevention, analytics, or customer support.

title: How We Use Personal Data
paragraphs: Axiorem uses personal data only for purposes reasonably connected to the Service, the relationship with the User or Customer, applicable legal obligations, security, and other disclosed purposes.
Depending on the context, Axiorem may use personal data to:
bullets: Provide the Service and requested features.
Process and transform Customer Content as instructed by the Customer.
Generate AI-assisted outputs and learning materials.
Manage Projects, Organizations, Users, roles, and permissions.
Process payments and maintain billing records.
Monitor and protect the security of the Service.
Detect, investigate, prevent, and respond to fraud, abuse, or security incidents.
Maintain appropriate business and technical records.
Comply with legal, regulatory, or governmental obligations.
Establish, exercise, or defend legal claims.
Perform other purposes disclosed to you at the time of collection or otherwise permitted by applicable law.

title: Legal Bases and Jurisdiction-Specific Processing Grounds
paragraphs: Depending on the jurisdiction, Axiorem may rely on different legal grounds or lawful bases for processing.
Potential grounds may include:
bullets: Performance of a contract or steps taken at your request before entering into a contract.
Legitimate interests, where permitted and appropriately balanced against applicable rights.
Consent, where required or voluntarily provided.
Other grounds recognized under applicable law.

title: AI Processing and Use of Customer Content
paragraphs: Axiorem uses AI, retrieval, embeddings, classification, summarization, generation, and related technologies to provide requested functionality.
Where necessary to provide an AI-enabled feature, appropriate portions of Customer Content may be transmitted to the relevant AI or model provider.
Axiorem's use of Customer Content for AI processing is limited by the applicable Service configuration, customer instructions, contractual commitments, provider settings, and applicable law.
Axiorem does not intend to treat Customer Content as a general-purpose public dataset merely because it is submitted to the Service.

Unless expressly stated otherwise in an applicable agreement, Axiorem should not represent that Customer Content is used to train foundation models without verifying the actual configuration and contractual terms of the relevant AI providers.

title: Our Approach to Customer Documents
paragraphs: Axiorem is designed around data minimization for source documents.

Subject to the actual production implementation, the intended workflow is that a Customer uploads a source document, temporary storage may be used to receive and process it, the document is ingested and chunked, the original active source file is removed from active cloud storage after successful processing, and the processed representation may remain associated with the relevant Project.
Deleting a Project is intended to remove associated processed representations, subject to applicable retention, backup, security, and legal limitations.

Axiorem does not state that a source document disappears from every technical system instantaneously. Temporary caches, backups, operational logs, provider-side processing, failed-job artifacts, and security systems may have different lifecycles where technically or legally necessary.

title: Cookies and Similar Technologies
paragraphs: Axiorem may use cookies, local storage, pixels, SDKs, or similar technologies necessary to operate the website or Service.
These technologies may be used for:
bullets: Analytics or marketing where separately enabled and permitted by law.

title: How We Share Information
paragraphs: Axiorem may disclose personal data only as reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Policy, the Terms, a DPA, or otherwise permitted or required by law.
Recipients may include:
bullets: Cloud hosting, storage, and infrastructure providers.
Analytics, monitoring, security, and support providers.
LMS and integration partners at the Customer's direction.
Professional advisors such as lawyers, accountants, auditors, or insurers.
Corporate transaction counterparties where legally permitted and appropriately protected.
Government authorities, courts, regulators, or law-enforcement bodies where disclosure is legally required or otherwise permitted.

paragraphs: Axiorem uses reasonable technical and organizational measures appropriate to the nature of the Service and the risks associated with processing personal data.

title: Privacy Incidents and Breach Response
paragraphs: Axiorem maintains an incident-response process intended to identify, contain, investigate, remediate, and document privacy and security incidents.
If Axiorem determines that an incident requires notification under applicable law or contract, Axiorem will provide notices in accordance with the applicable requirements.

Notification may depend on the type of data involved, the nature and severity of the incident, the likelihood of harm, applicable legal deadlines, contractual requirements, available facts, and whether disclosure would interfere with an investigation or security response.

title: Your Privacy Rights
paragraphs: Depending on where you live and the context in which your data is processed, you may have rights relating to personal data.
These may include:
bullets: Opting out of certain forms of processing.
Information about recipients or categories of recipients.
The right to complain to a competent authority.

title: India — Digital Personal Data Protection Framework
paragraphs: For India-facing processing, Axiorem intends to align its privacy practices with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ("DPDP Act") and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, to the extent and from the dates on which their provisions apply to the relevant processing.

The DPDP framework recognizes concepts including Data Principal, Data Fiduciary, Data Processor, notice, consent, withdrawal of consent, access, correction, erasure-related rights, grievance handling, and obligations concerning security and processing.

The exact operational obligations that apply to Axiorem depend on the commencement status, role, category of processing, and whether Axiorem is acting as a Data Fiduciary or Data Processor for a particular activity.

title: European Economic Area / UK
paragraphs: Where GDPR, EU Member State data-protection law, UK GDPR, or equivalent privacy rules apply, Axiorem intends to provide the disclosures required by the applicable regime.
Depending on the processing activity, those disclosures may include:
bullets: Identity and contact details of the relevant controller.
Contact details of a Data Protection Officer or representative where required.
Information about automated decision-making where applicable.

title: California and U.S. State Privacy Rights
paragraphs: Where applicable U.S. state privacy laws apply, Axiorem will provide the rights and disclosures required by those laws.
Depending on the applicable statute, these may include rights to:
bullets: Opt out of certain sale or sharing activities.
Limit certain uses of sensitive personal information.
Avoid unlawful discrimination for exercising privacy rights.
Use authorized agents or approved request mechanisms.

title: Children and Minors
paragraphs: Axiorem is primarily a business and workplace learning platform and is not intended to be directed to children.
Unless expressly stated otherwise, individuals below the minimum age permitted by applicable law should not create or use Accounts.

If Axiorem becomes aware that it has collected personal data from a child in circumstances where applicable law requires parental or guardian authorization, Axiorem may take appropriate steps to address the situation, including deletion where required.

title: Marketing Communications
paragraphs: Axiorem may send operational communications necessary to provide and secure the Service.
Where permitted, Axiorem may also send product updates, feature announcements, educational content, or marketing communications.
Recipients may opt out of non-essential marketing communications by using the unsubscribe mechanism provided in the communication or by contacting Axiorem.
Opting out of marketing communications does not necessarily stop transactional, security, or account-related messages.

title: Analytics and Product Improvement
paragraphs: Axiorem may use technical and usage information to understand Service performance, diagnose problems, improve usability, detect abuse, and improve the reliability of the platform.

Axiorem should distinguish between personal data used to operate the Service, aggregate or de-identified analytics, Customer Content, AI prompts and retrieved context, and information used for product improvement.

Customer Content should not be represented as being used for model training, product improvement, benchmarking, evaluation, or analytics unless that processing actually occurs and is permitted by the applicable legal and contractual framework.

title: Automated Decision-Making and Profiling
paragraphs: Axiorem may generate recommendations, classifications, assessments, or other AI outputs. These outputs are not automatically equivalent to legally significant automated decisions.

Axiorem does not intend for its general-purpose Service to make final decisions about a person's employment, healthcare, credit, insurance, legal rights, or similarly consequential matters without appropriate customer controls and human review.

Where applicable law provides rights concerning solely automated decisions, profiling, or high-impact uses of AI, Axiorem and the relevant Customer are responsible for determining which obligations apply to the particular use case.

title: Customer / Organization Responsibilities
paragraphs: When an Organization uses Axiorem to process personal information about other people, the Organization is responsible for:
bullets: Ensuring it has a lawful basis and appropriate authority.
Honoring requests and rights where the Organization is the responsible controller or fiduciary.
Ensuring that uploaded documents are lawfully obtained and used.
Complying with sector-specific and employment-related privacy requirements.

paragraphs: Axiorem may update this Privacy Policy to reflect changes in the Service, infrastructure, legal requirements, processing practices, or security measures.
The "Last Updated" date will identify the most recent version.
For material changes, Axiorem may provide additional notice where required, including by email, in-product notice, or other reasonable means.
If a change requires consent under applicable law, Axiorem will obtain that consent where required.

title: Complaints and Supervisory Authorities
paragraphs: If you have a concern regarding Axiorem's privacy practices, you should first contact Axiorem using the details above so that we can investigate and respond.
Where applicable law provides a right to complain to a supervisory authority, data-protection authority, regulator, or other competent body, you may exercise that right.
The appropriate authority depends on your location, the nature of the processing, and the applicable privacy regime.

title: Definitions
bullets: "Personal Data / Personal Information" means information relating to an identified or identifiable individual, or another category recognized by applicable law.
"Customer Content" means information supplied to Axiorem by or on behalf of a Customer, including documents and other materials uploaded to the Service.
"Data Principal" means the individual recognized as such under the applicable Indian data-protection framework.
"Data Fiduciary" and "Data Processor" have the meanings assigned under applicable Indian law, including the DPDP Act where relevant.
"Controller" and "Processor" have the meanings assigned under applicable European or UK data-protection law where relevant.
"Organization" means the company, institution, partnership, government entity, or other legal entity using Axiorem.
"Service" means the Axiorem software, website, APIs, AI functionality, training functionality, and related services.

title: Publication and Interpretation Notes
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy is intended to be accurate, transparent, and consistent with Axiorem's actual technical and business practices.

Before publication, Axiorem must verify the relevant implementation details and ensure that no statement in this Policy is interpreted as a commitment to a technical control that has not been implemented, tested, and documented.
Where applicable law requires greater rights or protections than those described here, applicable law controls.
